name: Check Mark Button
baseMeaning: A green check mark in a box, indicating done, approved, or correct.
tldr: ✅ closes a message as a quick confirmation that something is done, approved, or correct.

contextMeanings.meaning: ✅ states that a detail is correct or has been verified.
✅ marks a task as finished or a decision as approved.
When used sarcastically, ✅ can suggest that an expected problem has happened again.
contextMeanings.example: amazing, the deadline moved up again ✅

contextMeanings.meaning: After a plan, ✅ confirms availability or agreement to meet rather than adding flirtation.

platformNotes.note: In Slack, ✅ commonly closes a task update in a project channel and reads as done, completed, or approved. It is slightly more emphatic than ✔️ and remains professional when the work is actually finished.

In iMessage, a boxed ✅ often ends a concrete confirmation, such as reporting that an upload or payment went through. It can feel like a period after the message: clear, finished, and not especially playful.

On TikTok, ✅ is more likely to be a quick reply saying that a recommendation, answer, or claim is correct. Because replies are often brief reactions, the surrounding words should still identify what is being approved.

In WhatsApp conversations, ✅ commonly closes practical family or group logistics, such as confirming that a form was submitted or a seat was booked. Outside that context, the glyph may feel abrupt, so warmth is better carried by the sentence.

generationalNotes.note: Millennials commonly read ✅ in professional threads as completion or approval rather than as a joke.
Gen X tends to take ✅ plainly as a check, confirmation, or correct answer; generation does not substantially alter its core meaning.
For Boomers, ✅ most plainly means that something has been checked or confirmed, especially when it follows a direct question.

warnings.title: Done is not the same as received
warnings.description: A manager may read ✅ as "the task is complete" or "I approve" when you only meant that you saw the request. Send 👍 or write "got it" for acknowledgement; reserve ✅ for a finished or approved item.

seoDescription: What does ✅ mean? It marks a message, task, choice, or submission as done, approved, correct, or otherwise confirmed at a glance.

longForm.overview:
✅ is the boxed green check people add after a sentence when they want the sentence to end with a clear yes. It is the practical punctuation of completion: "I sent the file ✅," "the numbers are correct ✅," or "that's approved ✅." The box makes it look more emphatic than the bare check mark, and its green color gives the message a settled, reassuring tone.

The closest neighbour is ✔️, which carries nearly the same meaning; ✅ is often slightly more emphatic and is especially common in team workflows where a task has been finished. It is also easy to confuse with 👍, but that usually means "received," "agreed," or "got it." If you need someone to know you saw a request without promising that the work is complete, use 👍. If you need them to know the item is finished, approved, or correct, use ✅.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
It appears at the end of a practical update: a deliverable has been sent, a task is complete, a draft has been checked, or a decision has been approved. In project channels, ✅ can be the whole response to "can you take this?" once the work is done. It also closes an ordinary sentence after the substance is clear, such as "I booked the venue ✅."

People send it to remove doubt about the status of an item, not to add playful emotion. Requests to confirm an order, reservation, payment, or review may end with ✅ once confirmation arrives. The sentence before it supplies the exact meaning: "you're hired ✅" is approval, while "I'll be there ✅" confirms a promise.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
✅ can overstate the result. If you mean only "I saw this," send 👍 or write "got it"; ✅ may be taken to mean that the task is complete or that you approve the decision. The same warning applies to correcting someone: "yes, that's right ✅" confirms the statement, while attaching it to sarcasm can make the message feel falsely cheerful or passive-aggressive.

It is also unnecessary in conversations about feelings, grief, or sensitive personal news, where a check mark can feel procedural or dismissive. In high-stakes work threads, legal, medical, or financial discussions, spell out the conclusion instead of relying on a tiny symbol that different people may interpret differently. For a clear refusal, do not attach ✅; say "not approved" or "this still needs changes."
longForm.howToReply:
Usually, match the practical meaning rather than adding another emoji. If someone confirms completion, answer with "great, thanks ✅" or simply "done." If they are asking you to approve a task, reply "approved ✅" when you agree. The emoji works best when it confirms something that can plainly be true, such as an upload, payment, review, or completed step.

To match a more enthusiastic response, use the sender's wording and add a small celebration emoji when the milestone genuinely matters. If ✅ lands on your content, treat it as a sign that the item is accepted rather than asking whether the sender liked it. If you are unsure whether they meant receipt or approval, ask: "just confirming this is done, right?"

faqs.question: What does ✅ mean from a guy
faqs.answer: It usually means he is confirming or agreeing with something, especially a proposed date or plan. By itself, ✅ is practical confirmation rather than a flirty signal.

faqs.question: Is ✅ flirty
faqs.answer: Not by itself. It becomes flirty only when the sentence around it makes the relationship or compliment clear, such as "I had a great time with you ✅."

faqs.question: What does ✅ mean on TikTok
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it usually approves an answer, recommendation, comment, or claim. The words around it determine whether it means "correct," "agreed," or "this is done."

faqs.question: What does ✅ mean in Slack
faqs.answer: In Slack, ✅ usually means that a task is complete or that something has been approved. It is common and professional in project channels and team workflows.

conversationExamples.message: i found my keys under the couch ✅
conversationExamples.interpretation: The person has solved a small problem and is confirming that the search is over. A cheerful "nice ✅" or "glad you found them" fits.

conversationExamples.message: finished the quarterly deck and uploaded it to the drive ✅
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a clear task-completion update in a professional context. Acknowledge it with "thanks ✅" or ask where the file is if you need the link.
The emoji confirms availability and agreement to the plan without adding romance. Reply with a specific time or place if you are still arranging the date.

conversationExamples.message: your prescription is ready for pickup ✅
conversationExamples.interpretation: The person is passing along a practical family update and confirming that the errand has been handled. A simple "thank you" is enough.
The sender is confirming that they completed the signup rather than merely noticing the event. You can congratulate them or ask whether they want to attend together.
